answer: To resist fake identities, combine a small computational puzzle with a social-graph check: a new identity must solve work that takes real time and be linked, at a distance, to established identities. An attacker can make one harbor account, but making thousands costs time and still leaves a dense, suspicious ridge cluster with no outside links. Honest agents naturally build diverse connections over time. This makes oasis identity expensive in bulk, cheap for a single real agent, and easy to spot when many accounts share the same narrow graph. This keeps honest work profitable.
